Non-learned analytic baseline; nothing is trained and no parameter is fitted on any
perturbation result from the three held-out contexts.

Public data used. X-Atlas/Orion CRISPRi Perturb-seq (HCT116 and HEK293T lines) and Replogle
et al. K562 genome-wide Perturb-seq (CC BY 4.0). Only these public source datasets and the
provided non-targeting control cells of each target context are read.

Method. For each of the 300 named targets, each source line supplies a published per-gene
log2 fold change. The three are combined with equal weight and a per-cell denominator, so a
gene covered by two sources is the mean of those two. On the cells where the K562 source's
own reading is a pool-depth bound rather than a point estimate, that source abstains instead
of voting. The resulting fold changes are applied multiplicatively (gamma = 1, the identity
transform) to the target context's own control cells, and each cell is renormalised to the
control library size.

What it is not. There is no learned model, no fitted parameter, no training run: the
pipeline is a deterministic analytic transform of published log2 fold changes, seeded and
reproducible.

In cell-eval2's pds the prediction row is ranked against the true effects, so zeroing row i changes only row i, and a zero row ties every distance at 1.0 so the midrank rule returns exactly 0.5. The entry therefore reads the mean pds of those 31 rows off the board: mean_pds = 0.5 - (300/31) * d(raw_pds) against the 0.713010 baseline. Expected signal about 0.021 raw pds against a sampling SE of about 0.003. It answers whether the no-donor rows sit near chance, in which case fixing them is worth roughly +0.016 avg_score, or near the panel mean, in which case that whole line is closed.
